title: Nigeria UK Special Passport Intervention October 2026: Dates, Cities and Requirements
summary: The Nigeria Immigration Service and Nigeria High Commission London are running Phase 2 of the UK Special Passport Intervention from 6–30 October 2026 in Manchester, London, Cardiff and Aberdeen. This guide lists the official venues, documents and administrative charges.
feeNote: The Nigeria High Commission says the approved standard administrative charge for the intervention is £20. Lost, misplaced or damaged passport cases require a separate £150 High Commission postal order/e-payment in addition to the passport application payment.
timeline: Phase 2 runs 6–30 October 2026 in Manchester, London, Cardiff and Aberdeen.
requirements: Old passport booklet for every reissue, renewal or change-of-data application.
£20 postal order payable to the Nigeria High Commission or the High Commission's official e-payment confirmation.
For a lost, misplaced or damaged passport: the additional £150 High Commission postal order/e-payment required by the notice.
A prepaid Royal Mail C4 Special Delivery self-addressed envelope for return of the processed passport.
steps: Open the Nigeria High Commission London notice and use its official intervention appointment link rather than a link copied from social media.
Complete the normal passport application and payment process, then print the application form, payment receipt and appointment slip.
Choose the intervention city that matches your appointment: Manchester, London, Cardiff or Aberdeen, and reconfirm the venue before travelling.
Prepare the old passport booklet if the application is a renewal, reissue or change of data, plus the High Commission administrative payment and prepaid Royal Mail return envelope.
Attend the intervention appointment within the 6–30 October 2026 window and keep all receipts and tracking information until the processed passport is returned.
notes: Official Phase 2 venues are: Nigeria House, 23 Platt Lane, Manchester M14 5NE; 56–57 Fleet Street, London EC4Y 1JU; Western Leisure Centre, Ely, Cardiff CF5 5HJ; and Hilton Convention Centre, 13 Smithfield Road, Aberdeen AB24 4NR.
The High Commission separately warned that claims of an approved £70 administrative charge were incorrect; it states that the standard administrative charge remains £20.
This temporary intervention does not replace the normal NIS passport application itself. Applicants still need the passport application form, payment receipt and appointment slip.

title: Is INEC Voter Registration Open? October 2026 Status and Fake Website Warning
summary: INEC has warned Nigerians about a fake website claiming a new nationwide voter-registration window. The Commission said the nationwide registration exercise had ended on 26 July 2026, so voters should use only INEC's official domains and current portal notices.
feeLabel: No fee to check official INEC status
feeNote: Do not pay or submit personal data to a website merely because it claims to be an INEC registration portal. Start from inecnigeria.org or cvr.inecnigeria.org.
timeline: The fake-site warning was reported from INEC on 3 October 2026. Registration status can change in future, so check the official INEC portal before acting.
requirements: Use an official INEC domain such as inecnigeria.org or cvr.inecnigeria.org.
If checking an existing voter record, use the personal details already attached to that INEC registration.
Do not enter NIN, phone, address or other personal data into an unverified registration link.
steps: Open INEC's official website or Continuous Voter Registration portal directly instead of following a forwarded social-media or messaging-app link.
Read the current service notice before starting any registration action; INEC's October warning said the nationwide registration exercise had ended on 26 July 2026.
If you are already registered and only need your voter/PVC information, use the existing-voter services rather than attempting a new registration.
If a link claims a new registration window, confirm the announcement on INEC's own website or official contact centre before submitting personal information.
Close and report any page using an unrelated domain or free-blog address while presenting itself as an INEC registration portal.
notes: INEC specifically disowned a Blogspot-based website circulating with claims of a September 28–October 27 registration exercise.

The separate MyNigeriaGuide PVC-status page remains the canonical guide for checking an existing PVC record and collection centre; this page answers the different search intent of whether a new registration window is currently genuine.
MyNigeriaGuide does not provide political advice or candidate guidance; this page is limited to administrative voter-service safety.
